messages.content: Execute a multi-turn sequence of bash commands.

content.text: I need more detail before I start running anything — the sequence itself is what matters here, and I don't want to guess and start mutating your workspace.

questions.question: What should the multi-turn bash sequence actually do?

options.label: You'll paste the commands
options.description: You give me an explicit list (e.g. `pwd`, `ls -la`, `git status`, `npm test`). I run them one at a time, in order, reporting output after each.

options.label: Read-only project recon
options.description: I run a safe inspection sequence of my own: pwd, ls, git status/branch/log, dependency manifests, test config. No writes, no installs, nothing destructive.

options.label: Build / test / verify
options.description: I run install → lint → build → test in sequence, stopping at the first failure. This may modify lockfiles, caches, and build output.

questions.question: How careful should I be about side effects?

options.label: Ask before each mutating step
options.description: Anything that writes files, installs packages, or touches git gets a confirmation prompt first.

options.label: Read-only only
options.description: Refuse anything that changes state; just inspect and report.

options.label: Go ahead freely
options.description: Run the whole sequence without stopping, including writes/installs.

content.text:
No selection came back, so I'll default to the safe option: a **read-only recon sequence**, one command group per turn, no writes, no installs, no git mutations. You can redirect me at any point.

**Turn 1 — where am I and what's here:**

`Bash` is gated in this session — it needs an approval that has no channel to travel through, and I was already told not to retry it the same way. So I'll run the same recon sequence through the read-only filesystem tools instead. Same information, no shell.

**Turn 1 — location and top-level contents:**
A Rust project in a scratch temp directory. **Turn 2 — manifest and source layout:**

tools.name: Agent
tools.description: Launches a sub-agent with its own context to handle a self-contained search or task, and returns its final report. Use it for broad exploration that would otherwise fill this conversation with file dumps.

agent.description: Name of a custom agent defined in ~/.codape/agents/*.json. Takes precedence over subagent_type. An unknown name is an error that lists the configured names.

subagent_type.description: Built-in agent type (general_purpose, explore, plan, verification, claude_code_guide, statusline_setup), or a configured custom agent name.

writable.description: Whether the sub-agent may write files. false restricts it to read-only tools (Read, Grep, Glob). Defaults to true.

max_retries.description: Shorthand for retry_policy.max_retries when retry_policy is not supplied.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a shell command and returns its output. This is the way to inspect the machine and to run programs: list files, read what a service returns, check processes, ports, and environment variables.

- The shell starts in the directory the previous call left it in, so `cd` persists between calls. Exported variables and other shell state do not; pass a sequence to one command or use absolute paths.
- The shell is non-interactive. Anything that waits for input blocks until the timeout.
- `timeout` is in seconds (default 60, max 600). A foreground command still running at its timeout is not killed: it moves to the background and the call answers with a job handle instead of an error.
- `run_in_background` returns at once with `job_id`, `pid` and an `output_file` that is written while the command runs. Use it for a server or a long job: start it once, read the output with JobOutput and stop it with JobKill. Do not start a second copy to check on it, and do not use `ps`/`pkill`, which many images do not have. A background command runs until it exits; it stops only at its own `timeout` (when you set one) or through JobKill.

timeout.description: Seconds. Foreground: how long to wait before moving the command to the background (default 60, max 600). Background: stop the job after this many seconds (default: no limit).

run_in_background.description: Start the command as a background job and return its job id and output file

key.description: Config key to query or set

tools.name: CurrentDir
tools.description: Reports the session's current working directory.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description: Replaces an exact string in a file. `old_string` must match the file byte for byte and must be unique unless `replace_all` is set, so include enough surrounding text to identify one site. Read the file first: editing text you have not seen is a guess.

branch.description: Optional branch name for the worktree

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Finds files by glob pattern (for example `**/*.rs`) under `path` (default: the working directory) and returns the matching paths. Use it to learn the layout of a tree; use Grep to search inside files.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description: Searches file contents with a regular expression and returns the matches, the matching file names, or counts. Narrow the search with `path` and `glob`; `-A`, `-B`, `-C`, and `head_limit` control how much context and volume come back.

glob.description: Only search files matching this glob

tools.name: JobKill
tools.description: Stops a background shell job and every process in its process group: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a short grace period. The job is recorded as failed. Use it instead of `kill`/`pkill`, which many images do not have and which is easy to aim at the wrong process — `pkill -f` can match the shell that is running it.

tools.name: JobList
tools.description: Lists the background shell jobs started with Bash `run_in_background`: the job id, state, pid, start time, output file and the command. Use it to find again a job you started earlier — a server, a build, a test run — instead of `ps`, which many images do not have.

all.description: Include finished jobs as well as running ones (default false)

tools.name: JobOutput
tools.description: Reads the output of a background shell job started with Bash `run_in_background`. Returns the job's state and the last `tail_lines` lines of its output file. The file is written while the command runs, so calling this again shows the new output — this is how you check whether a server has started, instead of starting a second copy.

tail_lines.description: How many trailing lines to return (default 200)

tools.name: ListDir
tools.description: Lists the entries of a directory (default: the working directory). Use it before Glob when you do not yet know what the tree looks like.

server_url.description: MCP server URL to authenticate with

redirect_url.description: The full URL the browser was redirected to after approval. Its code and state are parsed and the state is verified against the pending flow.

code.description: Authorization code, when finishing by hand after the browser callback did not arrive

code_verifier.description: PKCE verifier returned by the earlier call that produced the auth_url (optional when a pending flow is on disk)

headless.description: Return the authorization URL immediately instead of opening a browser. Used by a headless session's re-authorization handler, which prints the URL for a person to open later.

wait_for_callback.description: In a headless call, bind the loopback callback port, print the URL and the SSH port-forward command on stderr, and wait for the browser callback instead of returning immediately. Used when the operator can forward the port over SSH.

callback_port.description: Loopback port for the OAuth callback (default 8765). Must match the port the person forwards.

tools.name: NotebookEdit
tools.description: Replaces, inserts, or deletes a single cell in a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb file).

tools.name: Read
tools.description: Reads a file and returns its contents with line numbers. `file_path` must be absolute. Reads up to 2000 lines by default; use `offset` and `limit` to page through a larger file. Prefer this over shelling out to `cat`: it handles binary detection and paging for you.

offset.description: Skip this many lines from the start

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read (default 2000)

args.description: Arguments to pass to the skill

blockedBy.description: Task IDs that must complete first

block.description: Wait for output file to exist

timeout.description: Max seconds to wait for output

tools.name: TodoWrite
tools.description: Records and updates the plan as a todo list. Use it to keep a multi-step task on track: mark the item you are working on `in_progress` and finish each one by `completed` before moving on.

query.description: Search query for tool name or description

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description: Searches the web and returns result titles and URLs. Use it for documentation, release notes, or a fact you cannot establish from the machine; quote or read the page with WebFetch before relying on it.

allowed_domains.description: Only include results from these domains

tools.name: Write
tools.description: Writes a file, creating it or replacing its contents entirely. Parent directories must already exist. Use Edit for a small change to an existing file; Write is for new files or a full rewrite.

store.description: which store to list; omit to list every store
which store to write to; personal and project stay on this machine, shared and org are classified before they are sent

key.description: what the memory is about; may be hierarchical ('backend/auth')

if_version.description: the version this write replaces, from memory_read; omit to write regardless
